days.title: Across the south
days.intro: The one transfer day, and it is a real one: ten hours of train across the whole width of Germany, broken by an hour and a half on the Bodensee and two in Freiburg.

seq.note: Through Munich and Memmingen. Nearly four hours — this is the long day.

seq.stn: The station is on the island, two minutes from the harbour.

legs.note: A lion and a lighthouse on the two moles, and the Alps behind the lake.
The old lighthouse, from 1180, with the coloured tiled roof.
The island's main street, painted and arcaded end to end.
Stepped gable, frescoed front, from 1436.
The oldest church on the lake, with the round tower beside it.

seq.note: Along the lake and through Switzerland. Passports where you can reach them.

seq.stn: Fifteen minutes straight down Eisenbahnstraße to the Minster, or tram 1.

legs.note: The tower is the only great Gothic spire finished in the Middle Ages.
A market round the cathedral every morning but Sunday. Eat a long red sausage.
Little water channels down every street. Step in one and the story says you marry a local.
The red merchants' hall on the south side of the square.
A thirteenth-century gate with a tram going through it.
The other gate, at the bottom of the old town.
The cathedral's original sculpture, brought indoors out of the weather.

seq.note: Change at Offenburg. The Deutschland-Ticket runs out at Kehl — the tram over the bridge is €2.

seq.stn: The cathedral is fifteen minutes from the station, straight through Place Kléber.

legs.note: The big central square, five minutes from the station.
Pink sandstone, and the tallest building on earth for two hundred years.
The tanners' quarter on the water, timber-framed and absurdly pretty.

steps.note: Change at Offenburg. The Deutschland-Ticket runs out at Kehl — the tram over the bridge is €2.

steps.title: Goodnight, Strasbourg
steps.say: Tomorrow: Alsace.

days.title: Alsace
days.holiday: German Unity Day. France is working normally; Germany is not, so Heidelberg will be quiet when you get there.
days.intro: The morning in Strasbourg, the afternoon in Colmar, and over the Rhine to Heidelberg in the evening.

legs.note: Pink sandstone, and the tallest building on earth for two hundred years.
The figures move at 12:30. Get there early or you will not see it.
The tanners' quarter on the water, timber-framed and absurdly pretty.
Three medieval towers on the canals at the end of Petite France.
Walk up onto the roof for the view back over the towers. Free.
The big central square, five minutes from the station.
The bishops' palace, now three museums in one building.

seq.note: Forty minutes down the Alsace plain.

seq.stn: Ten minutes from the station to the old town.

legs.note: The canal at the bottom of the old town, with the flat-bottomed boats.
Tall narrow houses with open lofts where the hides were dried.
1537, with the wooden gallery and the painted panels. The famous one.
The old customs house, where the town's business was done.
A hundred and six carved faces on one facade.
Colmar's cathedral in everything but name.
The Isenheim Altarpiece. Worth the whole day on its own.
He was born here and he made the Statue of Liberty.

seq.note: Back over the Rhine. Three changes, and the last one is the long one.

steps.say: 35 minutes, straight through.
steps.note: Forty minutes down the Alsace plain.

steps.say: 5 h 10 min here, until the 17:06 on. Ten minutes from the station to the old town.

steps.title: Little Venice
steps.say: The canal at the bottom of the old town, with the flat-bottomed boats.

steps.title: Quartier des Tanneurs

steps.title: Maison Pfister
steps.say: 1537, with the wooden gallery and the painted panels. The famous one.

steps.title: Koïfhus

steps.say: A hundred and six carved faces on one facade.

steps.title: Collégiale Saint-Martin
steps.say: Colmar's cathedral in everything but name.

steps.title: Unterlinden Museum
steps.say: The Isenheim Altarpiece. Worth the whole day on its own.

steps.title: Back to Gare de Colmar
steps.say: 13 min back to the station. Aim to be on the platform by 17:06.

steps.title: Train to Heidelberg
steps.say: 220 minutes and 3 changes — TER 96262, then TER 81398, then RB51, then RE73.

steps.say: Market square church with shops built into its outer walls.

steps.title: Goodnight, Heidelberg
steps.say: Tomorrow: Nuremberg, and in.

days.title: Nuremberg, and in
days.intro: A morning on the Neckar, four hours inside Nuremberg's walls, and the last train north.

seq.stn: Bus 33 up to the castle, or the funicular from Kornmarkt.
see: Marktplatz and Church of the Holy Spirit

legs.note: Red sandstone ruin above the town. Funicular from Kornmarkt.
1788. The bronze monkey at the end is for holding, and for luck.

legs.to: Marktplatz and Church of the Holy Spirit
legs.note: Market square church with shops built into its outer walls.
1.6 km of pedestrian street, the longest in Germany.
The small square below the castle with the gilded Madonna. The funicular leaves from the corner.

seq.note: ICE, one change. Three hours and twenty.

seq.stn: Out of the station and through the Königstor straight into the old town.

legs.note: You come out of the station straight into a medieval gate.
Craft courtyard inside the wall by the station. Touristy but pretty.
Huge Gothic church with Veit Stoß's Annunciation hanging in the choir.
The broad market square below the castle rock.
The gold fountain standing on the market square. Turn the brass ring for luck.
The older of the two great churches, below the castle.
Walls, a very deep well, and the roofs of the old town below.
The square below the castle where everyone sits out.
Where Dürer lived and worked, just below the castle gate.
The prettiest surviving half-timbered lane in the city.
Covered wooden bridge over the Pegnitz, with the hangman's house.
Three in a roll, or a dozen on a pewter plate at Bratwursthäusle.

seq.note: The last one. Three hours, direct.

milan/Piazza del Duomo.name: Piazza del Duomo
milan/Piazza del Duomo.note: Straight up from the metro. The whole square opens at once.

milan/Milan Cathedral.name: Milan Cathedral
milan/Milan Cathedral.note: Six hundred years to build, and every one of them visible on the front.

milan/The cathedral roof.name: The cathedral roof
milan/The cathedral roof.note: Up among the spires and the statues. Lift or stairs; go up if the queue is short.

milan/Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II.name: Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II
milan/Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II.note: The glass-roofed arcade beside the Duomo, from 1877.

milan/La Scala.name: La Scala
milan/La Scala.note: Plain outside on purpose. The museum gets you a look into the auditorium.

milan/Sforza Castle.name: Sforza Castle
milan/Sforza Castle.note: Fifteen minutes on from the Duomo. The courtyards are free to walk into.

milan/Santa Maria delle Grazie.name: Santa Maria delle Grazie
milan/Santa Maria delle Grazie.note: The Last Supper is here. It has to be booked weeks out, so this is the church, not the painting.

genoa/Via Garibaldi.name: Via Garibaldi
genoa/Via Garibaldi.note: A street of palaces, all UNESCO, ten minutes uphill from the station.

genoa/Palazzo Rosso.name: Palazzo Rosso
genoa/Palazzo Rosso.note: One of the palaces, opened up. Go to the roof terrace for the rooftops.
genoa/Palazzo Rosso.about: The Palazzo Brignole Sale or Palazzo Rosso is a house museum located in Via Garibaldi, in the historical center of Genoa, in Northwestern Italy. The palace is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site Genoa: Le Strade Nuove and the system of the Palazzi dei Rolli

genoa/San Lorenzo Cathedral.name: San Lorenzo Cathedral
genoa/San Lorenzo Cathedral.note: Striped black and white. A British shell from 1941 sits unexploded inside.

genoa/Piazza De Ferrari.name: Piazza De Ferrari
genoa/Piazza De Ferrari.note: The big fountain. Everything in the centre runs off this square.

genoa/The caruggi.name: The caruggi
genoa/The caruggi.note: The old town lanes — the densest medieval quarter in Europe, and dark at noon.

genoa/Porto Antico.name: Porto Antico
genoa/Porto Antico.note: Renzo Piano's rebuilt old harbour, five minutes down from the lanes.

genoa/Genoa Aquarium.name: Genoa Aquarium
genoa/Genoa Aquarium.note: The biggest in Italy. Half a day if you let it be.

genoa/Boccadasse.name: Boccadasse
genoa/Boccadasse.note: A fishing village swallowed by the city, still painted, 20 min by bus 31.
genoa/Boccadasse.about: Boccadasse is an old mariners' village of the Italian city of Genoa. It lies within the borders of the neighbourhood of Albaro.

smargherita/The harbour front.name: The harbour front
smargherita/The harbour front.note: Palms, painted houses and the boats. Five minutes down from the station.
smargherita/The harbour front.photoFile: Santa Margherita Ligure - Veduta del Porto (1901).jpg

smargherita/Villa Durazzo.name: Villa Durazzo
smargherita/Villa Durazzo.note: Terraced gardens above the town, free to walk into.
smargherita/Villa Durazzo.photoFile: Villa Durazzo Centurione (Santa Margherita Ligure) - facciata a mare 1 2023-04-27.jpg

smargherita/Basilica di Santa Margherita.name: Basilica di Santa Margherita
smargherita/Basilica di Santa Margherita.note: Gold and chandeliers, and open when everything else is shut.
smargherita/Basilica di Santa Margherita.photoFile: Basilica di Santa Margherita d'Antiochia (Santa Margherita Ligure) - facciata 2023-04-27.jpg

portofino/The Piazzetta.name: The Piazzetta
portofino/The Piazzetta.note: The postcard: the little square at the head of the harbour.

portofino/The harbour.name: The harbour
portofino/The harbour.note: Ochre and pink houses standing in the water. This is what you came for.

portofino/Chiesa di San Giorgio.name: Chiesa di San Giorgio
portofino/Chiesa di San Giorgio.note: Up the steps behind the harbour, with the first view back down.

portofino/Castello Brown.name: Castello Brown
portofino/Castello Brown.note: Higher again. The view from the terrace is the one in every photograph.
portofino/Castello Brown.about: Castello Brown is a historic house museum located above the harbour of Portofino, in northern Italy. The site has been used for military defence since Roman times.

portofino/The lighthouse walk.name: The lighthouse walk
portofino/The lighthouse walk.note: Fifteen minutes on past the castle to the point, through pines.
portofino/The lighthouse walk.photoFile: Foto dell'Ottica del Faro di Portofino.jpg

verona/Piazza Bra.name: Piazza Bra
verona/Piazza Bra.note: The huge square you come into from the station, with the Arena on it.
verona/Piazza Bra.about: Piazza Bra, often simply called The Bra, is the largest public square in Verona, Italy, situated in its historic city center. The name "Bra" derives from a corruption of braida, a term rooted in the Lombardic word breit, meaning 'wide' or 'broad'.

verona/The Arena.name: The Arena
verona/The Arena.note: Roman, from about AD 30, and still used for opera every summer.

verona/Scaliger Tombs.name: Scaliger Tombs
verona/Scaliger Tombs.note: Gothic tombs hanging in mid-air on wrought iron, in a little churchyard off Piazza dei Signori.
verona/Scaliger Tombs.about: The Scaliger Tombs is a group of five Gothic funerary monuments in Verona, Italy, celebrating the Scaliger family, who ruled in Verona from the 13th to the late 14th century.

verona/Juliet's House.name: Juliet's House
verona/Juliet's House.note: The balcony was added in 1936. Go for the courtyard, not the story.

verona/Piazza delle Erbe.name: Piazza delle Erbe
verona/Piazza delle Erbe.note: Frescoed houses round the old Roman forum. Best at night.
verona/Piazza delle Erbe.about: Piazza delle Erbe is a square in Verona, northern Italy. It was once the town's forum during the time of the Roman Empire.

verona/Torre dei Lamberti.name: Torre dei Lamberti
verona/Torre dei Lamberti.note: 84 m, and a lift most of the way. The whole city from the top.

verona/Ponte Pietra.name: Ponte Pietra
verona/Ponte Pietra.note: Roman arches on one side, rebuilt on the other after 1945.

verona/Castelvecchio.name: Castelvecchio
verona/Castelvecchio.note: The Scaligeri castle and its bridge, rebuilt brick by brick.
verona/Castelvecchio.about: Castelvecchio is a castle in Verona, northern Italy. It is the most important military construction of the Scaliger dynasty that ruled the city in the Middle Ages.

bolzano/Waltherplatz.name: Waltherplatz
bolzano/Waltherplatz.note: The main square, with the cathedral on the corner and cafés all round.

bolzano/Bolzano Cathedral.name: Bolzano Cathedral
bolzano/Bolzano Cathedral.note: Green and yellow tiled roof, Gothic spire.
bolzano/Bolzano Cathedral.about: Bolzano Cathedral, or the Cathedral of the Assumption of Mary is the parish church of Bolzano, capital of South Tyrol, and cathedral of the Diocese of Bozen-Brixen. While the Bishop has resided in Bozen since 1964, the cathedral and the cathedral chapter remai

bolzano/The Laubengasse.name: The Laubengasse
bolzano/The Laubengasse.note: Eight hundred years of arcades, the medieval merchant street.

bolzano/Obstmarkt.name: Obstmarkt
bolzano/Obstmarkt.note: The fruit market at the end of the arcades, open six days a week.

bolzano/Ötzi.name: Ötzi
bolzano/Ötzi.note: The iceman from 3300 BC, kept at minus six, and you can look at him.

bolzano/Dominikanerkirche.name: Dominikanerkirche
bolzano/Dominikanerkirche.note: Giotto-school frescoes in the cloister, and almost nobody in it.

bolzano/Talfer meadows.name: Talfer meadows
bolzano/Talfer meadows.note: The river walk under the vineyards, ten minutes from the square.
bolzano/Talfer meadows.photoFile: Talferwiesen in Bozen gegen den Altenberg.jpg

bolzano/Runkelstein Castle.name: Runkelstein Castle
bolzano/Runkelstein Castle.note: The largest secular medieval fresco cycle anywhere. 40 min out.

ortisei/The village centre.name: The village centre
ortisei/The village centre.note: Pedestrian, painted, and the Dolomites standing over the end of the street.
ortisei/The village centre.photoFile: Sacun udu da Pedroc a Urtijëi.jpg

ortisei/The woodcarvers.name: The woodcarvers
ortisei/The woodcarvers.note: Val Gardena has carved wood for four hundred years. The workshops are open.
ortisei/The woodcarvers.photoFile: Arpizadëur ziplà tl lën da Batista Walpoth Urtijëi.jpg

ortisei/St Ulrich parish church.name: St Ulrich parish church
ortisei/St Ulrich parish church.note: Baroque, and full of local carving as you would expect.
ortisei/St Ulrich parish church.photoFile: Autere Sacro Cuer Vijo Canins dlieja San Durich a Urtijëi.jpg

ortisei/Luis Trenker promenade.name: Luis Trenker promenade
ortisei/Luis Trenker promenade.note: A flat walk out of the village with the Sassolungo ahead of you.
ortisei/Luis Trenker promenade.photoFile: Dolomites Val Gardena from Mont de Seura.jpg

ortisei/Seceda.name: Seceda
ortisei/Seceda.note: Cable car to 2500 m and the tilted ridge everyone photographs. Two and a half hours.

ortisei/Alpe di Siusi.name: Alpe di Siusi
ortisei/Alpe di Siusi.note: Europe's largest high alpine meadow, straight up from the village.

scristina/Santa Cristina centre.name: Santa Cristina centre
scristina/Santa Cristina centre.note: Smaller and quieter than Ortisei, with the same mountains.
scristina/Santa Cristina centre.photoFile: Franz Demetz und Florian Mussner bei Kirrchtag in St. Ulrich.jpg

scristina/Chiesa di Santa Cristina.name: Chiesa di Santa Cristina
scristina/Chiesa di Santa Cristina.note: The white church on the meadow with the Sassolungo behind it.

scristina/Puez-Odle park.name: Puez-Odle park
scristina/Puez-Odle park.note: The Col Raiser cable car goes up into it. The best short walk in the valley.

scristina/The valley floor walk.name: The valley floor walk
scristina/The valley floor walk.note: The flat path along the stream between the two villages.

innsbruck/Maria-Theresien-Straße.name: Maria-Theresien-Straße
innsbruck/Maria-Theresien-Straße.note: The wide street with the Nordkette standing at the end of it.
innsbruck/Maria-Theresien-Straße.photoFile: Maria-Theresien-Straße in Innsbruck with Alpine Backdrop.jpg

innsbruck/Golden Roof.name: Golden Roof
innsbruck/Golden Roof.note: 2657 gilded copper tiles, put up in 1500 so an emperor could watch the square.

innsbruck/Innsbruck Cathedral.name: Innsbruck Cathedral
innsbruck/Innsbruck Cathedral.note: Baroque, two towers, and a Cranach Madonna over the altar.

innsbruck/Hofkirche.name: Hofkirche
innsbruck/Hofkirche.note: Twenty-eight giant bronze mourners standing round an empty tomb.

innsbruck/The Inn quay.name: The Inn quay
innsbruck/The Inn quay.note: The row of coloured houses on the far bank, with the mountains behind.

mittenwald/Ballenhausgasse.name: Ballenhausgasse
mittenwald/Ballenhausgasse.note: The lane behind Obermarkt, quieter and just as painted.

mittenwald/Kalvarienberg.name: Kalvarienberg
mittenwald/Kalvarienberg.note: Stations of the Cross up a wooded hill, 25 min for the valley view.

mittenwald/Obermarkt.name: Obermarkt
mittenwald/Obermarkt.note: The painted main street — Lüftlmalerei on nearly every facade.

mittenwald/St Peter and Paul.name: St Peter and Paul
mittenwald/St Peter and Paul.note: Baroque church with a painted tower you can see from the whole valley.

mittenwald/Violin Making Museum.name: Violin Making Museum
mittenwald/Violin Making Museum.note: Mittenwald has made violins since 1684. Small, and genuinely lovely.

mittenwald/Lautersee.name: Lautersee
mittenwald/Lautersee.note: Mountain lake above the town, an hour up through the forest. Swimmable in summer, freezing now.

mittenwald/Ferchensee.name: Ferchensee
mittenwald/Ferchensee.note: The quieter second lake, half an hour on from Lautersee through the trees.

mittenwald/Karwendel cable car.name: Karwendel cable car
mittenwald/Karwendel cable car.note: Up to 2244 m. A viewing platform over the whole range.

mittenwald/Leutaschklamm.name: Leutaschklamm
mittenwald/Leutaschklamm.note: Gorge walkway on steel catwalks over the water. 4 km from town.

mittenwald/Isar riverside.name: Isar riverside
mittenwald/Isar riverside.note: The river comes out of the Karwendel here, milky green and very cold. Flat walk at the east edge of town.

mittenwald/The painted houses.name: The painted houses
mittenwald/The painted houses.note: Lüftlmalerei — frescoes painted straight onto wet lime. Mittenwald has the best street of them in Bavaria.
mittenwald/The painted houses.about: Lüftlmalerei is a form of mural art that is native to villages and towns of southern Germany and Austria, especially in Upper Bavaria and in the Tyrol.

mittenwald/Matthias Klotz monument.name: Matthias Klotz monument
mittenwald/Matthias Klotz monument.note: He brought violin-making back from Padua in 1684 and the town has lived on it since. His statue faces the church.
mittenwald/Matthias Klotz monument.about: Matthias Klotz (1653–1743) was a luthier, a member of the Klotz family of violin makers that flourished in Mittenwald, Duchy of Bavaria as early as 1683.

mittenwald/Hoher Kranzberg.name: Hoher Kranzberg
mittenwald/Hoher Kranzberg.note: A small summit with a big view, and a chairlift most of the way up.

garmisch/Mohrenplatz.name: Mohrenplatz
garmisch/Mohrenplatz.note: The small square at the top of Ludwigstraße.

garmisch/Kurpark Garmisch.name: Kurpark Garmisch
garmisch/Kurpark Garmisch.note: Bandstand, flowerbeds and the Wetterstein behind them.

garmisch/Ludwigstraße.name: Ludwigstraße
garmisch/Ludwigstraße.note: Partenkirchen's old painted street. Prettier than the Garmisch half.

garmisch/Old St Martin.name: Old St Martin
garmisch/Old St Martin.note: Medieval frescoes inside, including a giant St Christopher.

garmisch/Partnachklamm.name: Partnachklamm
garmisch/Partnachklamm.note: Gorge cut 80 m deep. Walkway through the spray. 20 min walk to the entrance.

garmisch/Zugspitze.name: Zugspitze
garmisch/Zugspitze.note: Germany's highest point, 2962 m. Cog railway plus cable car. Half a day.

garmisch/Olympic ski stadium.name: Olympic ski stadium
garmisch/Olympic ski stadium.note: The 1936 jump. You can walk up to the top of the tower.
garmisch/Olympic ski stadium.about: Olympiaschanze was a ski jumping venue in St. Moritz, Switzerland, it was built in 1926 and closed in 2006.

garmisch/Eibsee.name: Eibsee
garmisch/Eibsee.note: Turquoise lake under the Zugspitze. A flat 7 km loop.

ettal/Ettal Abbey church.name: Ettal Abbey church
ettal/Ettal Abbey church.note: Benedictine abbey from 1330. The dome fresco is the thing to look up at.

ettal/Abbey shop and distillery.name: Abbey shop and distillery
ettal/Abbey shop and distillery.note: The monks' liqueur, beer and cheese, sold at the gate.

ettal/Schloss Linderhof.name: Schloss Linderhof
ettal/Schloss Linderhof.note: Ludwig II's small palace with the golden bedroom. Bus from Ettal.

munich/Odeonsplatz.name: Odeonsplatz
munich/Odeonsplatz.note: The Feldherrnhalle and the yellow Theatinerkirche.

munich/Theatinerkirche.name: Theatinerkirche
munich/Theatinerkirche.note: Butter-yellow outside, all white stucco inside.

munich/Karlsplatz and Neuhauser Straße.name: Karlsplatz and Neuhauser Straße
munich/Karlsplatz and Neuhauser Straße.note: The shopping street that runs from the station to Marienplatz.

munich/Michaelskirche.name: Michaelskirche
munich/Michaelskirche.note: Renaissance church on the way in; Ludwig II is buried in the crypt.
munich/Michaelskirche.about: St. Michael's is a Jesuit church in Munich, capital city of the state of Bavaria, Germany.

munich/Alter Hof.name: Alter Hof
munich/Alter Hof.note: The Wittelsbachs' first castle, a quiet courtyard most people walk past.
munich/Alter Hof.about: The Alter Hof in the center of Munich is the former imperial residence of Louis IV, Holy Roman Emperor and consists of five wings: Burgstock, Zwingerstock, Lorenzistock, Pfisterstock and Brunnenstock. Like most of the old town, it was rebuilt after being destr

munich/Marienplatz.name: Marienplatz
munich/Marienplatz.note: The heart of the city. Glockenspiel at 11:00 and 12:00.
munich/Marienplatz.about: Marienplatz is a central square in the city centre of Munich, Germany. It has been the city's main square since 1158.

munich/St Peter's tower.name: St Peter's tower
munich/St Peter's tower.note: 306 steps. The best view in Munich, straight down onto Marienplatz.

munich/Viktualienmarkt.name: Viktualienmarkt
munich/Viktualienmarkt.note: Open-air food market since 1807. Lunch here.

munich/Frauenkirche.name: Frauenkirche
munich/Frauenkirche.note: The two onion domes on the skyline. Free to enter.

munich/Residenz.name: Residenz
munich/Residenz.note: The Wittelsbach palace. The Antiquarium hall alone is worth it.

munich/Hofgarten.name: Hofgarten
munich/Hofgarten.note: Quiet formal garden behind the Residenz.

munich/English Garden.name: English Garden
munich/English Garden.note: Bigger than Central Park. Surfers on the Eisbach at the south end.

munich/Chinesischer Turm.name: Chinesischer Turm
munich/Chinesischer Turm.note: Beer garden under a wooden pagoda, in the middle of the park.

munich/Hofbräuhaus.name: Hofbräuhaus
munich/Hofbräuhaus.note: The famous beer hall. Loud, touristy, still fun once.

munich/Asamkirche.name: Asamkirche
munich/Asamkirche.note: A tiny baroque church squeezed between shops. Astonishing inside.

munich/Nymphenburg Palace.name: Nymphenburg Palace
munich/Nymphenburg Palace.note: Summer palace and park, 20 min by tram.

munich/Deutsches Museum.name: Deutsches Museum
munich/Deutsches Museum.note: The largest science and technology museum in the world.

munich/Oktoberfest.name: Oktoberfest
munich/Oktoberfest.note: On the Theresienwiese. In 2026 it runs to 4 October — expect big crowds.

rosenheim/Max-Josefs-Platz.name: Max-Josefs-Platz
rosenheim/Max-Josefs-Platz.note: The arcaded main square, painted in colours.

rosenheim/Mittertor.name: Mittertor
rosenheim/Mittertor.note: The last of the town gates, with the town museum inside it.

rosenheim/Ludwigsplatz.name: Ludwigsplatz
rosenheim/Ludwigsplatz.note: Runs on from Max-Josefs-Platz. Cafés and the evening crowd.

rosenheim/St Nikolaus.name: St Nikolaus
rosenheim/St Nikolaus.note: Gothic, with a baroque interior and a tall brick tower.

rosenheim/The Inn riverside.name: The Inn riverside
rosenheim/The Inn riverside.note: Ten minutes out of the centre to the green river and the bridge.

rosenheim/Lokschuppen.name: Lokschuppen
rosenheim/Lokschuppen.note: A roundhouse turned exhibition hall, and a good one.

berchtesgaden/Schlossplatz.name: Schlossplatz
berchtesgaden/Schlossplatz.note: The square at the top of the town, with the abbey on it.

berchtesgaden/Stiftskirche.name: Stiftskirche
berchtesgaden/Stiftskirche.note: Romanesque cloister, Gothic nave. The oldest thing here.

berchtesgaden/The Royal Palace.name: The Royal Palace
berchtesgaden/The Royal Palace.note: The Wittelsbachs' last private house, still furnished as they left it.

berchtesgaden/Salt mine.name: Salt mine
berchtesgaden/Salt mine.note: Overalls, a wooden slide and a train into the mountain. Two hours.

berchtesgaden/Dokumentation Obersalzberg.name: Dokumentation Obersalzberg
berchtesgaden/Dokumentation Obersalzberg.note: What the Nazi leadership did on this mountain, told plainly, on the site.

berchtesgaden/Eagle's Nest.name: Eagle's Nest
berchtesgaden/Eagle's Nest.note: 1834 m, reached by bus and a brass lift through the rock. Half a day.

konigssee/The lakeshore.name: The lakeshore
konigssee/The lakeshore.note: Walled in by the Watzmann. The water is green and completely still.

konigssee/St Bartholomä.name: St Bartholomä
konigssee/St Bartholomä.note: The red onion domes on the far shore, reached only by the electric boat.
konigssee/St Bartholomä.about: Sankt Bartholomä is a municipality in the district of Graz-Umgebung in the Austrian state of Styria.

konigssee/Malerwinkel.name: Malerwinkel
konigssee/Malerwinkel.note: A short marked loop to the painters' corner, for the view back down the lake.

salzburg/Mirabell Gardens.name: Mirabell Gardens
salzburg/Mirabell Gardens.note: Ten minutes from the station, and the first thing you reach. Free.

salzburg/Makartsteg.name: Makartsteg
salzburg/Makartsteg.note: The footbridge over the Salzach, with the fortress straight ahead.

salzburg/Getreidegasse.name: Getreidegasse
salzburg/Getreidegasse.note: The wrought-iron shop signs, one after another, the length of the street.

salzburg/Mozart's birthplace.name: Mozart's birthplace
salzburg/Mozart's birthplace.note: Number 9, the yellow house. He was born on the third floor.

salzburg/Residenzplatz.name: Residenzplatz
salzburg/Residenzplatz.note: The big square with the baroque fountain, between the palace and the cathedral.

salzburg/Salzburg Cathedral.name: Salzburg Cathedral
salzburg/Salzburg Cathedral.note: Mozart was baptised here and played the organ in it.

salzburg/St Peter's Abbey.name: St Peter's Abbey
salzburg/St Peter's Abbey.note: The cemetery under the cliff is the quietest corner in the city.

salzburg/Hohensalzburg.name: Hohensalzburg
salzburg/Hohensalzburg.note: The biggest intact castle in central Europe. Funicular up from Kapitelplatz.

lindau/The harbour.name: The harbour
lindau/The harbour.note: A lion and a lighthouse on the two moles, and the Alps behind the lake.

lindau/Mangturm.name: Mangturm
lindau/Mangturm.note: The old lighthouse, from 1180, with the coloured tiled roof.
lindau/Mangturm.photoFile: Lindau Marina with Mangturm tower, Lindau, Germany, 20250502 0925 8506.jpg

lindau/Maximilianstraße.name: Maximilianstraße
lindau/Maximilianstraße.note: The island's main street, painted and arcaded end to end.

lindau/St Peter and the Diebsturm.name: St Peter and the Diebsturm
lindau/St Peter and the Diebsturm.note: The oldest church on the lake, with the round tower beside it.
lindau/St Peter and the Diebsturm.photoFile: Torre del ladrón, Lindau, Alemania, 2022-10-22, DD 41.jpg

freiburg/Freiburg Minster.name: Freiburg Minster
freiburg/Freiburg Minster.note: The tower is the only great Gothic spire finished in the Middle Ages.

freiburg/Münsterplatz market.name: Münsterplatz market
freiburg/Münsterplatz market.note: A market round the cathedral every morning but Sunday. Eat a long red sausage.

freiburg/The Bächle.name: The Bächle
freiburg/The Bächle.note: Little water channels down every street. Step in one and the story says you marry a local.

freiburg/Historisches Kaufhaus.name: Historisches Kaufhaus
freiburg/Historisches Kaufhaus.note: The red merchants' hall on the south side of the square.
freiburg/Historisches Kaufhaus.photoFile: Das historische Kaufhaus in Freiburg im Breisgau (2025).jpg

freiburg/Martinstor.name: Martinstor
freiburg/Martinstor.note: A thirteenth-century gate with a tram going through it.

freiburg/Schwabentor.name: Schwabentor
freiburg/Schwabentor.note: The other gate, at the bottom of the old town.
freiburg/Schwabentor.about: The Schwabentor, also called Obertor in the Middle Ages, is the more recent of the two remaining city gates of the medieval defensive wall of Freiburg im Breisgau in Baden-Württemberg, Germany.

freiburg/Augustinermuseum.name: Augustinermuseum
freiburg/Augustinermuseum.note: The cathedral's original sculpture, brought indoors out of the weather.

freiburg/Schlossberg.name: Schlossberg
freiburg/Schlossberg.note: Funicular or twenty minutes up, for the whole city and the Vosges beyond.

strasbourg/Place Kléber.name: Place Kléber
strasbourg/Place Kléber.note: The big central square, five minutes from the station.

strasbourg/Strasbourg Cathedral.name: Strasbourg Cathedral
strasbourg/Strasbourg Cathedral.note: Pink sandstone, and the tallest building on earth for two hundred years.

strasbourg/The astronomical clock.name: The astronomical clock
strasbourg/The astronomical clock.note: The figures move at 12:30. Get there early or you will not see it.
strasbourg/The astronomical clock.about: The Strasbourg astronomical clock is located in the Cathédrale Notre-Dame of Strasbourg, Alsace, France. It is the third clock on that spot and dates from the time of the first French possession of the city (1681–1870).

strasbourg/La Petite France.name: La Petite France
strasbourg/La Petite France.note: The tanners' quarter on the water, timber-framed and absurdly pretty.

strasbourg/Ponts Couverts.name: Ponts Couverts
strasbourg/Ponts Couverts.note: Three medieval towers on the canals at the end of Petite France.
strasbourg/Ponts Couverts.about: The Ponts Couverts are a set of three bridges and four towers that make up a defensive work erected in the 13th century on the River Ill in Strasbourg, France. The three bridges cross the four river channels of the Ill that flow through Strasbourg's historic P

strasbourg/Barrage Vauban.name: Barrage Vauban
strasbourg/Barrage Vauban.note: Walk up onto the roof for the view back over the towers. Free.
strasbourg/Barrage Vauban.about: The Barrage Vauban, or Vauban Dam, is a bridge, weir and defensive work erected in the 17th century on the River Ill in Strasbourg, France. At that time, it was known as the Great Lock, although it does not function as a navigation lock in the modern sense of

strasbourg/Palais Rohan.name: Palais Rohan
strasbourg/Palais Rohan.note: The bishops' palace, now three museums in one building.

strasbourg/Place de la République.name: Place de la République
strasbourg/Place de la République.note: The German imperial quarter — a completely different city, ten minutes away.

colmar/Koïfhus.name: Koïfhus
colmar/Koïfhus.note: The old customs house, where the town's business was done.

colmar/Maison Pfister.name: Maison Pfister
colmar/Maison Pfister.note: 1537, with the wooden gallery and the painted panels. The famous one.

colmar/Collégiale Saint-Martin.name: Collégiale Saint-Martin
colmar/Collégiale Saint-Martin.note: Colmar's cathedral in everything but name.

colmar/Maison des Têtes.name: Maison des Têtes
colmar/Maison des Têtes.note: A hundred and six carved faces on one facade.

colmar/Quartier des Tanneurs.name: Quartier des Tanneurs
colmar/Quartier des Tanneurs.note: Tall narrow houses with open lofts where the hides were dried.

colmar/Little Venice.name: Little Venice
colmar/Little Venice.note: The canal at the bottom of the old town, with the flat-bottomed boats.
colmar/Little Venice.photoFile: Petite Venise depuis le pont de la rue des Écoles (Colmar) (8).jpg

colmar/Unterlinden Museum.name: Unterlinden Museum
colmar/Unterlinden Museum.note: The Isenheim Altarpiece. Worth the whole day on its own.

colmar/Bartholdi Museum.name: Bartholdi Museum
colmar/Bartholdi Museum.note: He was born here and he made the Statue of Liberty.

heidelberg/Heidelberg Castle.name: Heidelberg Castle
heidelberg/Heidelberg Castle.note: Red sandstone ruin above the town. Funicular from Kornmarkt.

heidelberg/Philosophers' Walk.name: Philosophers' Walk
heidelberg/Philosophers' Walk.note: Across the river and up. The classic view back at the castle.

heidelberg/Old Bridge.name: Old Bridge
heidelberg/Old Bridge.note: 1788. The bronze monkey at the end is for holding, and for luck.

heidelberg/Hauptstraße.name: Hauptstraße
heidelberg/Hauptstraße.note: 1.6 km of pedestrian street, the longest in Germany.

heidelberg/Marktplatz and Church of the.name: Marktplatz and Church of the Holy Spirit
heidelberg/Marktplatz and Church of the.note: Market square church with shops built into its outer walls.

heidelberg/Student Prison.name: Student Prison
heidelberg/Student Prison.note: Where misbehaving students were locked up — and covered the walls in graffiti.

heidelberg/The Great Tun.name: The Great Tun
heidelberg/The Great Tun.note: A wine barrel holding 220,000 litres, inside the castle. There is a dance floor on top of it.

heidelberg/German Pharmacy Museum.name: German Pharmacy Museum
heidelberg/German Pharmacy Museum.note: Also in the castle, and included — four centuries of jars, stills and alarming remedies.

heidelberg/Jesuitenkirche.name: Jesuitenkirche
heidelberg/Jesuitenkirche.note: White and enormous inside, a block off the Hauptstraße.

heidelberg/University Square.name: University Square
heidelberg/University Square.note: The old university, the Lion Fountain, and students everywhere since 1386.

heidelberg/Kornmarkt.name: Kornmarkt
heidelberg/Kornmarkt.note: The small square below the castle with the gilded Madonna. The funicular leaves from the corner.

heidelberg/Karlstor.name: Karlstor
heidelberg/Karlstor.note: The triumphal gate at the east end of the Hauptstraße.

heidelberg/Königstuhl funicular.name: Königstuhl funicular
heidelberg/Königstuhl funicular.note: Continue past the castle to the top of the hill.

nuremberg/Königstor and the walls.name: Königstor and the walls
nuremberg/Königstor and the walls.note: You come out of the station straight into a medieval gate.

nuremberg/Schöner Brunnen.name: Schöner Brunnen
nuremberg/Schöner Brunnen.note: The gold fountain standing on the market square. Turn the brass ring for luck.
nuremberg/Schöner Brunnen.about: Schöner Brunnen is a 14th-century fountain located on Nuremberg's main market next to the town hall and is considered one of the main attractions of the city's Historical Mile. The fountain is approximately 19 metres high and has the shape of a Gothic spire.

nuremberg/Sebalduskirche.name: Sebalduskirche
nuremberg/Sebalduskirche.note: The older of the two great churches, below the castle.

nuremberg/Tiergärtnertorplatz.name: Tiergärtnertorplatz
nuremberg/Tiergärtnertorplatz.note: The square below the castle where everyone sits out.

nuremberg/Heilig-Geist-Spital.name: Heilig-Geist-Spital
nuremberg/Heilig-Geist-Spital.note: A hospital built out over the river on arches.

nuremberg/Imperial Castle.name: Imperial Castle
nuremberg/Imperial Castle.note: Walls, a very deep well, and the roofs of the old town below.

nuremberg/Hauptmarkt.name: Hauptmarkt
nuremberg/Hauptmarkt.note: The broad market square below the castle rock.

nuremberg/Albrecht Dürer's House.name: Albrecht Dürer's House
nuremberg/Albrecht Dürer's House.note: Where Dürer lived and worked, just below the castle gate.

nuremberg/Weißgerbergasse.name: Weißgerbergasse
nuremberg/Weißgerbergasse.note: The prettiest surviving half-timbered lane in the city.

nuremberg/Henkersteg.name: Henkersteg
nuremberg/Henkersteg.note: Covered wooden bridge over the Pegnitz, with the hangman's house.

nuremberg/Frauenkirche.name: Frauenkirche
nuremberg/Frauenkirche.note: On the market square. The clock figures move at noon.

nuremberg/St Lorenz.name: St Lorenz
nuremberg/St Lorenz.note: Huge Gothic church with Veit Stoß's Annunciation hanging in the choir.

nuremberg/Germanisches Nationalmuseum.name: Germanisches Nationalmuseum
nuremberg/Germanisches Nationalmuseum.note: The biggest museum of German culture. Enormous.

nuremberg/Documentation Centre.name: Documentation Centre
nuremberg/Documentation Centre.note: The Nazi rally grounds, honestly explained. 15 min by tram.

nuremberg/Nuremberg sausages.name: Nuremberg sausages
nuremberg/Nuremberg sausages.note: Three in a roll, or a dozen on a pewter plate at Bratwursthäusle.

nuremberg/Handwerkerhof.name: Handwerkerhof
nuremberg/Handwerkerhof.note: Craft courtyard inside the wall by the station. Touristy but pretty.

berlin/Brandenburg Gate.name: Brandenburg Gate
berlin/Brandenburg Gate.note: The obvious one, and still worth standing in front of.

berlin/Gendarmenmarkt.name: Gendarmenmarkt
berlin/Gendarmenmarkt.note: Two matching cathedrals and the concert hall. The handsomest square in Berlin.

berlin/Museum Island.name: Museum Island
berlin/Museum Island.note: Five museums on one island. The Pergamon's Ishtar Gate is the highlight.
berlin/Museum Island.about: The Museum Island is a museum complex on the northern part of Spree Island in the historic heart of Berlin, Germany. It is one of the capital's most visited sights and one of the most important museum sites in Europe.

berlin/Reichstag dome.name: Reichstag dome
berlin/Reichstag dome.note: Free, but you must register online in advance.

berlin/Berlin Cathedral.name: Berlin Cathedral
berlin/Berlin Cathedral.note: Climb to the dome walkway for the view over the island.

berlin/Memorial to the Murdered Jews of.name: Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe
berlin/Memorial to the Murdered Jews of.note: 2711 concrete slabs. Walk into the middle of it.

berlin/Tiergarten.name: Tiergarten
berlin/Tiergarten.note: The big central park, with the Victory Column in the middle.

berlin/Alexanderplatz TV Tower.name: Alexanderplatz TV Tower
berlin/Alexanderplatz TV Tower.note: 368 m. Book a time slot to skip the queue.
berlin/Alexanderplatz TV Tower.about: The Fernsehturm in central Berlin was constructed between 1965 and 1969 by the government of the German Democratic Republic as both a functional broadcasting facility and a symbol of communist power.

berlin/Checkpoint Charlie.name: Checkpoint Charlie
berlin/Checkpoint Charlie.note: The old crossing point. Busy and a bit tacky, but it is the spot.

berlin/Charlottenburg Palace.name: Charlottenburg Palace
berlin/Charlottenburg Palace.note: The largest palace in Berlin, with a big park behind it.

berlin/Hackesche Höfe.name: Hackesche Höfe
berlin/Hackesche Höfe.note: Eight linked courtyards of shops and cafés in Mitte.

presets.name: Abu Dhabi to Berlin
presets.sub: Genoa · Portofino · Verona · Val Gardena · Mittenwald · Salzburg · Alsace

tickets.name: Milano Centrale → Genova Piazza Principe
tickets.detail: IC 685, 18:55 → 20:44, direct. Carriage 3, seats 5C and 5D. Me&You fare.

tickets.name: Genova Piazza Principe → Verona Porta Nuova
tickets.detail: RV 3075, 15:44 → 19:17, one change. Seats reserved. Ordinaria.

tickets.name: Malpensa Express, airport → Milano Centrale
tickets.detail: Every 30 minutes from Terminal 1, 50 minutes. About €13 each. Buy at the machine in arrivals — no need to book ahead, but know it exists before you go looking for a bus.

tickets.name: South Tyrol — Mobilcard, 1 day
tickets.detail: Covers the 350 and 354 buses up Val Gardena and every other bus and train in South Tyrol. €22 each. Ask the Bolzano hotel first: many hand out a free Südtirol Guest Pass that does the same thing.
tickets.cost: €44 for two, or free with the Guest Pass

tickets.name: Bolzano → Innsbruck → Mittenwald
tickets.detail: Three countries in one morning. Book the ÖBB Sparschiene as early as you can — it is about €20 each booked ahead and roughly double on the day.

tickets.name: Deutschland-Ticket, October
tickets.detail: €58 each a month, and it covers every regional train and bus in Germany from 1 October: Rosenheim, Berchtesgaden, the Königssee buses, Lindau, Freiburg, up to the border at Kehl, Heidelberg. It is a calendar-month subscription, so it does nothing for 29 and 30 September — cover those two days with a Bayern-Ticket each instead.

tickets.name: Bayern-Ticket, 29 and 30 September
tickets.detail: €34 for the first person plus about €10 for the second, per day. Covers Mittenwald, Garmisch, the 326 bus to Ettal, Munich and Rosenheim. Does not start until 09:00 on a weekday.

tickets.name: The hop into Austria
tickets.detail: The Deutschland-Ticket dies at the border: bus 840 is covered only as far as Zollhäuser. Buy the Austrian end from the driver — about €4 each — or take the train to Freilassing on the D-Ticket and a €3.50 single on to Salzburg Hbf.

tickets.name: Strasbourg tram D, from Kehl
tickets.detail: The D-Ticket takes you Freiburg → Offenburg → Kehl, right up to the border. Tram D runs from Kehl station into the middle of Strasbourg in fifteen minutes. About €2.10 each, bought at the stop.

tickets.name: Alsa+ Groupe Journée
tickets.detail: €39.10 for up to five people, all Alsace trains, trams and buses for the day. It is only sold for Saturdays, Sundays and holidays — and 3 October is a Saturday. Covers Strasbourg to Colmar and back, and the tram out to Kehl where the D-Ticket picks you up again.

tickets.name: Heidelberg → Nuremberg → Berlin
tickets.detail: The last day is the only one the Deutschland-Ticket cannot carry — regional trains would take eleven hours. Two ICE legs. Book the Sparpreis the moment the plan is fixed; it is roughly €30 each booked early against €80 on the day.
